audit.whatIsWrong: The lane read misattributed his shield to his passive.
audit.why: Indestructible is his W (12/11/10/9/8s), not his passive; his passive is Darkness Rise, a damage aura that switches on after 3 hits. Dodging Obliterate to "deny the shield" is the wrong instruction — dodging it denies Darkness Rise stacks, which is what actually makes his early brawl scary.
audit.corrected: early and wants.foe[0] now separate Darkness Rise (3 hits, damage aura) from Indestructible (W shield).

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described with no ultimate cooldown, and Death’s Grasp was called a shield.
audit.why: Realm of Death is 140/120/100s — his single kill button on a two-and-a-half-minute timer early, which is exactly why every other stage is yours. Death's Grasp (E, 16s at rank 1) is a pull, not a shield.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid and late now carry 140s; early names Death’s Grasp correctly as the pull.

audit.whatIsWrong: The anti-heal decision was written as "Grievous doesn’t help much against his shield" — a negative that also happens to be wrong.
audit.why: Riot's text for Indestructible: "Mordekaiser stores damage he deals and takes to create a shield. He may consume the shield to heal." The shield converts to a HEAL, so Grievous Wounds is directly relevant. This is the one item decision in the matchup.
audit.corrected: late now says anti-heal is worth it and explains why.

edits.before: You hold the edge at levels 1-2. Mordekaiser wants to land Q Obliterate and hit you with abilities to stack his passive Indestructible shield, so sidestep his Q to deny it and don't feed his shield for free — do that and your brawl beats his early. He has no gap-closer besides E Death's Grasp pull, so respect being yanked into his Q, but he can't out-fight you here. Farm for a lead, chip his shield down, and press toward your level 3 spike.
edits.after: You hold the edge at levels 1-2. Mordekaiser wants to land Obliterate (Q) and hit you with abilities — three hits on you switches on Darkness Rise, his damage aura — so sidestep the Q and don't feed it for free. Do that and your brawl beats his early. His only gap-closer is Death's Grasp (E), which pulls you in, so respect being yanked into Obliterate, but he can't out-fight you here. Farm for a lead and press toward level 3.

edits.before: Stack Indestructible shield with Q and E hits
edits.after: Land 3 hits to turn on Darkness Rise, then Q

edits.before: Sustain through your drain with Death's Grasp shield uptime
edits.after: Store damage into Indestructible, then eat the shield to heal

edits.before: Respect his R Realm of Death — it isolates you into a 1v1 death realm where he steals your stats; don't fight at 6 with cooldowns down, and save Flash/E to survive the duration.
edits.after: Respect Realm of Death (R) — a 140s isolation into a 1v1 realm where he steals your stats. Don't fight at 6 with cooldowns down, and save Flash and E to survive the duration.

edits.before: Levels 3 through 5 stay firmly yours: with your full Q pattern and drain you out-trade him before and during his early item timing, landing Q3 sweetspot into E and healing through his damage. The one phase that flips is level 6 — his R Realm of Death drags you into an isolated 1v1 where he steals a chunk of your stats and turns the duel in his favor, so do not fight at 6 unless your cooldowns and Flash are up. Track his R; when it's down, you're back in control.
edits.after: Levels 3 through 5 stay firmly yours: with your full Q pattern and drain you out-trade him before and during his early item timing, landing Q3 sweetspot into E and healing through his damage. The one phase that flips is level 6 — Realm of Death drags you into an isolated 1v1 where he steals a chunk of your stats, so do not fight at 6 unless your cooldowns and Flash are up. It is 140s at rank 1; when it's down, you're back in control.

edits.before: From first item on the lane returns to you and stays there. Post-Eclipse your drain plus World Ender heal-amp wins every extended brawl, and as a durable fighter you out-scale him — his R is genuinely his only reliable kill button. The whole late game is cooldown tracking: bait or wait out Realm of Death, then all-in. Grievous doesn't help much against his shield, so rely on raw combo damage and sustained trades rather than trying to burst him.
edits.after: From first item on the lane returns to you and stays there. Post-Eclipse your drain plus World Ender heal-amp wins every extended brawl, and as a durable fighter you out-scale him — Realm of Death is genuinely his only reliable kill button. The whole late game is counting that 140s. Anti-heal is worth it: Indestructible converts stored damage into a heal, so cutting the heal cuts his whole sustain plan.

notes: The old late-game line "Grievous doesn't help much against his shield" was a false negative and is replaced. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
